exposure: Early life prevention strategy (antenatal education, nutrition supplement, smoke avoidance, control of delivery mode, feeding)
Maternal nutrition conditions (folic acid and vitamin D intake)
cohort: The study enrolled 502 infants born in the hospital between January 2014 to July 2015, along with 132 infants (<1 year) diagnosed with bronchial asthma as a positive control group.
finding: An early life prevention strategy significantly reduced the incidence rate of infant bronchial asthma, as well as rates of wheezing, eczema, and respiratory tract infection.
mod_finding: Delivery mode for mothers was identified as an independent risk factor for bronchial asthma, and the vaginal delivery rate was remarkably higher in the prevention group.
